summary:
Breuil, Hellmann and Schraen describe the completed local rings of the **trianguline variety** X_tri(r̄) at points of integral weight in terms of the completed local rings of a scheme built from **Grothendieck’s simultaneous resolution**, and draw local and global consequences.

The local model is the scheme X = g̃ ×_g g̃, where g̃ = {(gB,ψ) : Ad(g⁻¹)ψ ∈ b} and q : g̃ → g is the simultaneous resolution. Its irreducible components X_w are indexed by the Weyl group; §2 proves they are reduced, Cohen–Macaulay (Bezrukavnikov–Riche) and — new here — **normal**, and computes cycles on the Steinberg variety through Beilinson–Bernstein and Kazhdan–Lusztig theory. The bridge is Fontaine’s theory of **almost de Rham** B_dR-representations: W ↦ (D_pdR(W), ν_W) is an equivalence onto pairs (vector space, nilpotent operator), Galois-stable B⁺_dR-lattices correspond to filtrations, and a trianguline (φ,Γ_K)-module supplies a second flag. A point of X_tri(r̄) therefore determines a triple (two flags, nilpotent operator), i.e. a point x_pdR of X, and the main local theorem (3.33) says that X̂_tri(r̄)_x and X̂_{w,x_pdR} agree up to formally smooth morphisms. Since the X_w are normal and Cohen–Macaulay, so is X_tri(r̄) at such points (Corollary 3.7.10), hence it is locally irreducible.

The local applications are: flatness of the character and weight maps, the accumulation property, a tangent-space bound that recovers and sharpens the authors’ earlier estimate, the determination of **all** local companion points in the crystalline case (Theorem 4.2.3: exactly the w with w_x ≼ w), and a locally analytic **Breuil–Mézard type** statement (Conjecture 4.3.4, proved for generic crystalline r in Theorem 4.3.8) expressing the cycle of the fibre of X_tri(r̄) over a character as a combination Σ_Π m_{δ,Π}C_{r,Π} with multiplicities from locally analytic principal series.

Globally, for a definite unitary group under the usual Taylor–Wiles hypotheses and via the patched eigenvariety, they prove (i) **classicality**: every generic crystalline strictly dominant point of the Hecke eigenvariety comes from a classical automorphic form; (ii) **companion constituents**: all constituents predicted by Breuil’s conjecture occur in the completed cohomology, so all expected companion points exist; and (iii) **singularities**: the eigenvariety is Cohen–Macaulay with flat weight map at such a point, and is singular there whenever w_xw_0 is not a product of distinct simple reflections. The last is the first systematic source of singular points on eigenvarieties.

items.name: Global setting: definite unitary group and its Hecke eigenvariety
items.statement: F⁺ is totally real, F an imaginary quadratic extension of F⁺, G a unitary group in n variables over F⁺ splitting over F and over all p-adic places of F⁺ and compact at all infinite places; S_p the places of F⁺ above p; L/Q_p finite and large enough. Ŝ(U^p,L)^an is the space of overconvergent p-adic automorphic forms of tame level U^p, an admissible locally Q_p-analytic representation of G(F⁺⊗_Q Q_p) ≅ ∏_{v|p} GL_n(F⁺_v). S is a finite set of finite places containing S_p and the v ∤ p where U_v is not hyperspecial, m^S a maximal ideal of the Hecke algebra with Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S} ≠ 0, and ρ̄ : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(F̄_p) the associated mod p representation, assumed irreducible. Y(U^p,ρ̄) is the rigid analytic Hecke eigenvariety over L parametrising the finite-slope systems of Hecke eigenvalues in Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S}; a point is a pair (ρ,δ) with ρ a deformation of ρ̄ and δ a locally Q_p-analytic character of the diagonal torus of G(F⁺⊗_Q Q_p).

items.name: Crystalline generic points, the permutations w and w_x, strict dominance
items.statement: A point x = (ρ,δ) is crystalline generic if for every v|p: ρ_v is crystalline; the eigenvalues (φ_{v,i}) of φ^{q_v} on D_cris(ρ_v) satisfy φ_{v,i}φ_{v,j}^{−1} ∉ {1, q_v} for i ≠ j, q_v the residue cardinality of F⁺_v; and the Hodge–Tate weights of ρ_v are regular. To such an x one attaches two elements w = (w_v)_v and w_x = (w_{x,v})_v of S := ∏_{v|p} S_n^{[F⁺_v:Q_p]}: w measures the relative position of the weights of the δ_{v,i} in the antidominant order, w_x the relative position of the two flags coming from the p-adic Hodge theory of ρ_v. x is strictly dominant when w = w_0, equivalently when the algebraic weight of δ is dominant. x′ = (ρ,δ′) is a companion point of x = (ρ,δ) when δ′δ^{−1} is Q_p-algebraic.

items.name: The standing Taylor–Wiles hypotheses (i)–(iv)
items.statement: (i) p > 2; (ii) F/F⁺ is unramified, F contains no non-trivial p-th root of 1, and G is quasi-split at all finite places of F⁺; (iii) U_v is hyperspecial at every finite place v of F⁺ inert in F; (iv) ρ̄(Gal(F̄/F(ᵖ√1))) is adequate in the sense of [66, Def. 2.20].

items.name: Remark 1.1: the missing hypothesis in the authors’ earlier papers
items.statement: The authors record that the assumption ᵖ√1 ∉ F was omitted in a first version of this paper and is also missing in the global results of [19] and [20]: it should be added to [19, Th. 1.5 and Th. 3.5] and all subsequent results, and to [20, Th. 1.1] and the results of [20, §3 and §5]. All results of [19] and [20] remain true with the more general notion of adequate subgroup of [66, Def. 2.20] in place of [65, Def. 2.3].
items.note: This is the authors’ own correction to their two earlier published papers, not to the present one; recorded here because it changes the hypotheses any roadmap must carry for those results.

items.name: Theorem 1.2: classicality of crystalline strictly dominant points
items.statement: Assume (i)–(iv). If x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) is generic crystalline strictly dominant, then x comes from a classical automorphic form of G(A_{F⁺}); in particular ρ is automorphic. Strict dominance is needed for x itself to be classical, but if x is generic crystalline and not strictly dominant there is a generic crystalline strictly dominant x′ = (ρ,δ′) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄), so ρ is automorphic in any case.

items.name: Theorem 1.3: eigenvarieties are singular at sufficiently critical points
items.statement: Assume (i)–(iv) and U^p small enough. If x ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) is generic crystalline strictly dominant and w_xw_0 is not a product of pairwise distinct simple reflections, then x is a singular point of Y(U^p,ρ̄).

items.name: Theorem 1.4: all expected companion constituents occur
items.statement: Assume (i)–(iv) and U^p small enough. If ρ : Gal(F̄/F) → GL_n(L) comes from a generic crystalline strictly dominant point x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄), then all the companion constituents associated to ρ in [15, §6] and [16, Conj. 6.1] occur, up to twist, as G(F⁺⊗_Q Q_p)-subrepresentations of Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S}[m_ρ]. In particular all companion points x_{w′} of x with w_x ≼ w′ exist in Y(U^p,ρ̄).

items.name: Generic characters of ((F⁺_v)^×)^n
items.statement: A character δ of ((F⁺_v)^×)^n is generic if δ_iδ_j^{−1} and δ_iδ_j^{−1}|·|_v are not Q_p-algebraic characters of (F⁺_v)^× for i ≠ j, |·|_v the norm character.

items.name: The patched eigenvariety and the trianguline variety
items.statement: All the statements hold with Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S} replaced by the patched locally Q_p-analytic representation Π^an_∞ of [23] and Y(U^p,ρ̄) by the patched eigenvariety X_p(ρ̄) of [19, §3.2], which exist only under (i)–(iv). By [19, §3.6], X_p(ρ̄) is a union of irreducible components of 𝔛_{ρ̄^p} × ∏_{v|p} X_tri(ρ̄_v) × U^g, where 𝔛_{ρ̄^p} is the rigid generic fibre of the framed deformation space at the places of S∖S_p, U^g an open polydisc, and X_tri(ρ̄_v) the trianguline variety at v.

items.name: Theorem 1.5: the trianguline variety is normal and Cohen–Macaulay at such points
items.statement: Let x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(ρ̄_v) with δ generic locally algebraic with distinct weights. Then X_tri(ρ̄_v) is normal, hence irreducible, and Cohen–Macaulay in an affinoid neighbourhood of x.

items.name: The point x_pdR and the local model map
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 1.5, r is almost de Rham in the sense of Fontaine and so is every deformation of r over a nilpotent thickening of L. Fontaine’s equivalence W ↦ (D_pdR(W), ν_W) identifies almost de Rham B_dR-representations with pairs (D,N), N nilpotent, and Galois-stable B⁺_dR-lattices with separated exhaustive ν_W-stable filtrations of D_pdR(W), complete flags when the Sen weights are multiplicity free. With g the Lie algebra of G := (Res_{F⁺_v/Q_p} GL_{n/F⁺_v})_L, b that of the upper Borel, g̃ := {(gB,ψ) ∈ G/B × g : Ad(g^{−1})ψ ∈ b} is smooth irreducible of dimension dim G and g̃ → g is Grothendieck’s simultaneous resolution; X := g̃ ×_g g̃ is equidimensional of dimension dim G with irreducible components X_{w′} indexed by the Weyl group. The two ν-stable flags of D_pdR(r_dR) — the one from the triangulation and the Hodge filtration — give x_pdR := (𝒟_•, Fil_•, N) ∈ X(L), and one obtains a map X̂_tri(ρ̄_v)_x → X̂_{x_pdR} factoring through X̂_{w,x_pdR}.

items.name: Theorem 1.6: the local model theorem
items.statement: For x as in Theorem 1.5, the formal schemes X̂_tri(ρ̄_v)_x and X̂_{w,x_pdR} are isomorphic up to formally smooth morphisms.

items.name: Theorem 1.7: the components X_{w′} are normal and Cohen–Macaulay
items.statement: The algebraic varieties X_{w′} are normal and Cohen–Macaulay for every w′. The Cohen–Macaulay property is due to Bezrukavnikov–Riche; the normality (Theorem 2.3.6) is new to the authors’ knowledge.

items.name: Theorem 1.8: all local companion points in the crystalline case
items.statement: Let x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(ρ̄_v) be as in Theorem 1.5 and crystalline strictly dominant, and let w_x measure the relative position of 𝒟_• and Fil_•. The local companion points of x — the x′ = (r,δ′) ∈ X_tri(ρ̄_v) with δ′δ^{−1} Q_p-algebraic — are parametrised by the w′ with w_x ≼ w′.

items.name: Cycles on the framed deformation ring and the fibres of the trianguline variety
items.statement: R_r is the complete local ring of framed deformations of r over local artinian L-algebras of residue field L, and Z(Spec R_r) the free abelian group on the irreducible closed subschemes; for A a quotient of R_r, [Spec A] := Σ_{𝔭 minimal} m(𝔭,A)[Spec A/𝔭] with m(𝔭,A) the length of A_𝔭 (1.1). For δ generic, (r′,δ′) ↦ r′ gives a closed immersion Spec Ô_{X_tri(ρ̄_v),(r,δ)} ↪ Spec R_r, and X_tri(ρ̄_v)_δ denotes the fibre of the character map above δ, again with a closed immersion into Spec R_r. Although X_tri(ρ̄_v) is reduced, the fibre X_tri(ρ̄_v)_δ can be highly non-reduced and can carry Kazhdan–Lusztig multiplicities.

items.name: Theorem 1.9: a locally analytic Breuil–Mézard type cycle decomposition
items.statement: For any crystalline generic deformation r of ρ̄_v with distinct Hodge–Tate weights and any absolutely irreducible constituent Π of a locally Q_p-analytic principal series of GL_n(F⁺_v), there is a unique cycle 𝒞_{r,Π} of codimension [F⁺_v:Q_p]·n(n+3)/2 in Z(Spec R_r) such that for all locally Q_p-analytic characters δ, [Spec Ô_{X_tri(ρ̄_v)_δ,(r,δ)}] = Σ_Π m_{δ,Π} 𝒞_{r,Π}, where the left-hand side is 0 if (r,δ) ∉ X_tri(ρ̄_v) and m_{δ,Π} is the multiplicity of Π in the principal series induced from δ suitably normalised.

items.name: The rank-two example: a reducible weight fibre and a ramified weight map
items.statement: For n = 2, F⁺_v = Q_p and r = χ₁ ⊕ χ₂ with χ_i = z^{h_i}unr(φ_i), h₁ < h₂, put δ₁ = z^{h₂}unr(φ₁), δ₂ = z^{h₁}unr(φ₂). Then X_tri(ρ̄_v) is smooth at (r,(δ₁,δ₂)) while Spec Ô_{X_tri(ρ̄_v)_{(δ₁,δ₂)},(r,(δ₁,δ₂))} is reduced with two irreducible components of dimension 3, one from crystalline deformations and one from trianguline non-crystalline ones; the induced principal series has two constituents Π₁ (locally algebraic) and Π₂, and 𝒞_{r,Π₁}, 𝒞_{r,Π₂} are the two component cycles, while for the other ordering 𝒞_{r,Π′₂} = 0. Non-irreducibility of the fibre implies that the projections of X_tri(ρ̄_v) to the character space and to the weight space are not smooth at that point.

items.name: The two cycle identities behind Theorem 1.4
items.statement: For ρ as in Theorem 1.4 and x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) ↪ X_p(ρ̄) generic crystalline strictly dominant, write x_{w′} = (ρ,δ_{w′}) for the companion point attached to w′ ≽ w_x and Π_{w′} for the irreducible socle of the principal series induced from δ_{w′}. With M_∞ the coherent Cohen–Macaulay sheaf of [20, Lem. 3.8] and M̂_{∞,wt(δ),x} its pull-back to the weight fibre, (1.2) [M̂_{∞,wt(δ),x}] = Σ_{w_x ≼ w′} P_{1,w_0w′}(1)[L(w′)] with L(w′) ≠ 0 if and only if Hom(Π_{w′}, Π^an_∞[m_ρ]) ≠ 0, and (1.3) [Ô_{X_p(ρ̄)_{wt(δ)},x}] = Σ_{w_x ≼ w′} P_{1,w_0w′}(1)𝒞(w′) with the 𝒞(w′) non-zero cycles of codimension [F⁺:Q]·n(n+1)/2; 𝒞(w_0) is irreducible and [L(w_0)] ∈ Z_{≥0}𝒞(w_0). (1.2) is representation theory and does not use the local model; (1.3) does.

items.name: Split reductive G in good characteristic, and the Schubert cells
items.statement: G is a split connected reductive group over a field k of good characteristic (char k = 0, or char k > h with h the Coxeter number; only char k = 0 is used later), B ⊃ T a Borel and maximal torus, U the unipotent radical, W = N_G(T)/T with longest element w_0, length lg and Bruhat order ≼; g, b, t, u the Lie algebras and w·λ = w(λ+ρ) − ρ the dot action. G acts diagonally on G/B × G/B, and for w ∈ W with a lift ẇ, U_w := G·(1,ẇ)B×B is a locally closed subscheme, smooth of dimension dim G − dim B + lg(w), with G/B × G/B = ∐_w U_w.

items.name: g̃ and the simultaneous resolution
items.statement: g̃ := {(gB,ψ) ∈ G/B × g : Ad(g^{−1})ψ ∈ b} (2.1) is a closed subscheme of dimension dim G, and G ×^B b ≅ g̃ by (g,ψ) ↦ (gB, Ad(g)ψ) (2.2), so g̃ → G/B is a vector bundle and g̃ is smooth and irreducible, a subvector bundle of the trivial bundle G/B × g. The map q : g̃ → g, (gB,ψ) ↦ ψ, is Grothendieck’s simultaneous resolution of singularities. g^reg and g^{reg−ss} denote the regular and regular semisimple loci and g̃^reg, g̃^{reg−ss} their preimages.

items.name: Properties of the simultaneous resolution
items.statement: q is proper and surjective; its restriction to q^{−1}(g^reg) is quasi-finite; and its restriction to q^{−1}(g^{reg−ss}) is étale of degree |W|.

items.name: The scheme X = g̃ ×_g g̃ and the maps π, κ₁, κ₂
items.statement: X := g̃ ×_g g̃ = {(g₁B,g₂B,ψ) ∈ G/B × G/B × g : Ad(g_i^{−1})ψ ∈ b, i = 1,2} (2.3), with π : X → G/B × G/B the projection (2.4) and κ_i : X → t, (g₁B,g₂B,ψ) ↦ image of Ad(g_i^{−1})ψ under b ↠ t (2.5). For w ∈ W, V_w := π^{−1}(U_w).

items.name: V_w → U_w is a vector bundle
items.statement: The projection V_w → U_w induced by π is a geometric vector bundle of relative dimension dim B − lg(w); for y = (gB,gẇB) ∈ U_w the fibre is Ad(g)(t ⊕ (u ∩ Ad(ẇ)u)), an affine space of that dimension (2.6)–(2.7).

items.name: Intersection of two subvector bundles of constant fibre dimension
items.statement: Let V → Y be a geometric vector bundle over a reduced scheme locally of finite type over a field and W₁, W₂ ⊆ V subvector bundles such that for every closed point y the intersection of the fibres is an affine space of constant dimension r. Then the scheme-theoretic intersection W₁ ∩ W₂ is a geometric vector bundle of rank r.

items.name: The closed subsets X_w and the Bruhat constraint
items.statement: X_w is the Zariski closure of V_w in X. For w, w′ ∈ W, X_w ∩ V_{w′} ≠ ∅ implies w′ ≼ w, since π(X_w) is the closure Ū_w of the Schubert cell.

items.name: X is a local complete intersection with components X_w
items.statement: X is locally a complete intersection and its irreducible components are the X_w, w ∈ W; in particular X is Cohen–Macaulay and dim X = dim X_w = dim g = dim G. X ⊆ G/B × G/B × g is equidimensional of dimension dim G and cut out by 2 dim u equations in a smooth scheme.
items.note: Its proof cites "Lemma 2.2.1" for what is Proposition 2.2.1; see source issue E6.

items.name: X is reduced and pr_i restricts to a resolution of g̃
items.statement: X is reduced, hence so is each component X_w with its scheme structure as the scheme-theoretic image of the open stratum. For i = 1,2 the projection pr_i : X → g̃ induces a proper birational morphism pr_{i,w} : X_w → g̃ which is an isomorphism above g̃^reg.

items.name: Equidimensionality of the fibres of κ_i
items.statement: For i = 1,2 the fibres of κ_i and of κ_{i,w} := κ_i|_{X_w} are equidimensional of dimension dim G − dim T, and the restriction of κ_i to each irreducible component of X is surjective. The proof uses the G_m-action λ·(g₁B,g₂B,ψ) = (g₁B,g₂B,λψ) and the description of π^{−1}(U_w) ∩ κ₁^{−1}(0) as a vector bundle over U_w with fibre u ∩ Ad(w)u.

items.name: Miracle flatness
items.statement: Let f : Y → Z be a morphism of noetherian schemes with Z regular, Y Cohen–Macaulay and all fibres equidimensional of dimension dim Y − dim Z. Then f is flat.

items.name: X_w is Cohen–Macaulay and the weight maps are flat
items.statement: The schemes X_w are Cohen–Macaulay and the morphisms κ_i and κ_{i,w} are flat for i = 1,2. In characteristic > h this is Bezrukavnikov–Riche; the characteristic-zero case is obtained by spreading out over Z_{(p)} with a Chevalley model.

items.name: κ₂ = Ad(w^{−1})∘κ₁ on X_w
items.statement: For w ∈ W one has κ_{2,w} = Ad(w^{−1}) ∘ κ_{1,w}, so that the square formed by κ_{1,w}, κ_{2,w} and the two projections t → t/W commutes (2.9).

items.name: (π,κ_i) is smooth on V_w with irreducible fibres
items.statement: For w ∈ W the fixed subscheme t^w ⊂ t of Ad(w) is smooth and irreducible. The restriction of (π,κ_i) : X → G/B × G/B × t to V_w is a smooth map V_w → U_w × t with irreducible fibres; in particular V_w ∩ κ_i^{−1}(t^{w′}) is irreducible for all w, w′.

items.name: The components X_w are normal
items.statement: The schemes X_w are normal. Since they are Cohen–Macaulay it suffices to prove regularity in codimension one; a codimension-one component C of X_w ∖ V_w would lie in V_{w′} ∩ κ₁^{−1}(t^{ww′^{−1}}) for some w′, and codimension counting forces ww′^{−1} to be a reflection s_α with lg(w′) < lg(s_αw′), whence C meets pr_{1,w}^{−1}(g̃^reg), where X_w is smooth.
items.note: The paper states this normality is new; it is what makes the trianguline variety normal at the points of Corollary 3.7.10.

items.name: Conjecture 2.3.7 on the strata of X_w
items.statement: CONJECTURE (not proved in this paper). For w, w′ ∈ W with w′ ≼ w and w̃ = ww′^{−1}, X_w ∩ V_{w′} = V_{w′} ∩ κ₁^{−1}(t^{w̃}). Lemma 2.3.4 gives the inclusion ⊆.
items.note: A conjecture, not a theorem: it must not be planned as a target. Remark 2.5.4 and Remark 4.1.6(iii) record what it would give.

items.name: The Steinberg variety and the Springer resolution
items.statement: Assume char k = 0. With g/G := Spec(R_g^G) and t/W ≅ g/G, let κ̄ : X → g/G be the composite of X → g with g ↠ g/G. Z := (κ̄^{−1}(0))^red (2.11) is the Steinberg variety, and Z ≅ Ñ ×_𝒩 Ñ where 𝒩 is the nilpotent cone, Ñ := {(gB,ψ) ∈ G/B × 𝒩 : Ad(g^{−1})ψ ∈ u} ≅ G ×^B u (2.12) and Ñ → 𝒩 is the Springer resolution. V′_w := π^{−1}(U_w) ∩ Z and Z_w is its closure with the reduced structure.

items.name: Components of the Steinberg variety
items.statement: Z is equidimensional of dimension dim G − dim T and its irreducible components are the Z_w, w ∈ W.

items.name: What is not known about the Z_w
items.statement: Contrary to the X_w, it does not seem to be known whether the components Z_w of the Steinberg variety are Cohen–Macaulay, and even granting that, the proof of Theorem 2.3.6 does not extend; the authors do not know whether the Z_w are normal.

items.name: Top-dimensional cycles on Z and the class of a scheme
items.statement: Z⁰(Z) is the free abelian group on the irreducible components of Z, so the [Z_w] form a basis and Z⁰(Z) ≅ Z[W]. For Y whose space is a union of components of Z, [Y] := Σ_w m(Z_w,Y)[Z_w] (2.13) with m(Z_w,Y) the length of O_{Y,η_w} at the generic point of Z_w. X̄_w := κ_{1,w}^{−1}(0) (not reduced) has every component of dimension exactly dim Z, hence of the form Z_{w′}.

items.name: Category O, Verma modules and Kazhdan–Lusztig multiplicities
items.statement: O is the BGG category of U(g)-modules attached to g ⊃ b ⊃ t, M(μ) = U(g) ⊗_{U(b)} k(μ) the Verma module of highest weight μ and L(μ) its unique irreducible quotient. The constituents of M(ww_0·0) are the L(w′w_0·0), with multiplicity P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1), P_{x,y} the Kazhdan–Lusztig polynomials; P_{x,y} ≠ 0 iff x ≼ y and P_{x,x}(1) = 1, so L(w′w_0·0) occurs in M(ww_0·0) iff w′ ≼ w.

items.name: The Beilinson–Bernstein equivalence and the D-modules 𝔐, 𝔏
items.statement: O(0) is the block of trivial infinitesimal character. The Beilinson–Bernstein correspondence gives an exact equivalence BB_G : O(0) ≅ D−Mod^{rh}_{G/B×G/B} onto regular holonomic G-equivariant D-modules on G/B × G/B, obtained from the usual B-equivariant equivalence on G/B by extending along gB ↦ (B,gB). One writes 𝔐(ww_0·0) and 𝔏(ww_0·0) for the images of M(ww_0·0) and L(ww_0·0).

items.name: Characteristic varieties lie in the Steinberg variety
items.statement: Z is the union inside T^*(G/B × G/B) of the conormal bundles of the diagonal G-orbits U_w, and Z_w is the closure of T^*_{U_w}(G/B × G/B). For 𝔐 regular holonomic G-equivariant, Ch(𝔐)^red ⊆ Z, so the characteristic cycle [𝔐] := [Ch(𝔐)] ∈ Z⁰(Z) is defined and additive.
items.locator: Proposition 2.4.4 with the surrounding text, printed pp. 321–322

items.name: The Kazhdan–Lusztig irreducibility conjecture is false in general
items.statement: Kazhdan and Lusztig conjectured for G = SL_n that [𝔏(ww_0·0)] = Z_w, i.e. that the characteristic cycles are irreducible; this is false for n ≥ 8 and true for n ≤ 7.

items.name: The fibre X̄_w is the characteristic cycle of the Verma D-module
items.statement: For w ∈ W, [X̄_w] = [𝔐(ww_0·0)] in Z⁰(Z).

items.name: Three bases of Z⁰(Z) and the multiplicity matrices
items.statement: (i) The families ([Z_w]), ([𝔐(ww_0·0)]) and ([𝔏(ww_0·0)]) are bases of Z⁰(Z). (ii) [𝔐(ww_0·0)] = Σ_{w′} P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1)[𝔏(w′w_0·0)]. (iii) There are integers a_{w,w′} ∈ Z_{≥0} with [𝔏(ww_0·0)] = Σ_{w′} a_{w,w′}[Z_{w′}], a_{w,w} = 1, a_{w,w′} = 0 unless w′ ≼ w, and a_{w,w′} = 0 whenever w′ ≺ w and U_{w′} lies in the smooth locus of Ū_w. Consequently X̄_w contains every Z_{w′} with w′ ≼ w, in general with multiplicities.
items.note: Its proof prints "P_{w,w′}(1) = 0 unless w′ ≼ w", dropping the w₀ prefixes; see source issue E7.

items.name: The characteristic cycle is invariant under the parabolic P_w
items.statement: Let P_w ⊆ G be the largest parabolic containing B whose Levi M_w makes ww_0·0 dominant for M_w ∩ B; the B-action on L(ww_0·0) extends to P_w. Then [𝔏(ww_0·0)] ∈ Z⁰(Z) is invariant under every element of P_w(k), and consequently h(Z_{w′}) = Z_{w′} for every h ∈ P_w(k) whenever a_{w,w′} ≠ 0.

items.name: The scheme T = t ×_{t/W} t and its components
items.statement: By Lemma 2.3.4 the map (κ₁,κ₂) : X → t × t factors through T := t ×_{t/W} t. The irreducible components of T are the T_w = {(z, Ad(w^{−1})z) : z ∈ t}, and X_w is the unique component of X with (κ₁,κ₂)(X_w) = T_w.

items.name: The completion detects the component
items.statement: Let x be a closed point of X and w ∈ W with x ∈ X_w. For w′ ∈ W, the composite X̂_{w,x} ↪ X̂_x → T̂_{(κ₁,κ₂)(x)} factors through T̂_{w′,(κ₁,κ₂)(x)} if and only if w′ = w. The proof uses that for an excellent local reduced ring whose quotients by the minimal primes are normal, completion induces a bijection on minimal primes — which is where the normality of Theorem 2.3.6 enters.
items.note: Its proof prints the ambient scheme of η̂_{T_w} as Spec Ô_{X,x} instead of Spec Ô_{T,(κ₁,κ₂)(x)}; see source issue E7.

items.name: Tangent-space bound and a smoothness criterion for X_w
items.statement: Let x ∈ X_w be a closed point whose image in g is 0 and w′ ∈ W with x ∈ X_w ∩ V_{w′}. (i) dim T_{X_w,x} ≤ dim T_{Ū_w,π(x)} + dim t^{ww′^{−1}} + lg(w′w_0). (ii) If t^{ww′^{−1}} has codimension lg(w) − lg(w′) in t and Ū_w is smooth at π(x), then X_w is smooth at x. Granting Conjecture 2.3.7 for w = w_0, the inequality in (i) is an equality for w = w_0.

items.name: Cycles commute with completion, and the completed KL decomposition
items.statement: For a coherent module ℳ on X̄ := κ₁^{−1}(0) and a closed point x of X̄, [ℳ̂_x] = Σ_w m(Z_w,ℳ)[Spec Ô_{Z_w,x}] in Z⁰(Spec Ô_{Z,x}) (Lemma 2.5.5). Setting [𝔏̂(ww_0·0)_x] := Σ_{w′} a_{w,w′}[Spec Ô_{Z_{w′},x}] (2.16), one obtains [Ô_{X̄_w,x}] = Σ_{w′} P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1)[𝔏̂(w′w_0·0)_x] (Corollary 2.5.6).

items.name: B_dR-representations and almost de Rham representations
items.statement: A B_dR-representation of G_K is a finite dimensional B_dR-vector space with a continuous semilinear G_K-action; every one contains a G_K-stable B⁺_dR-lattice. W is almost de Rham if it contains a G_K-stable B⁺_dR-lattice W⁺ whose associated C-representation W⁺/tW⁺ has all Sen weights in Z; de Rham implies almost de Rham. The almost de Rham representations form a tannakian subcategory Rep_pdR(G_K) stable under kernels, cokernels and extensions.

items.name: The rings B⁺_pdR, B_pdR, the derivation ν and the functor D_pdR
items.statement: B⁺_pdR := B⁺_dR[log t] and B_pdR := B_dR ⊗_{B⁺_dR} B⁺_pdR, with G_K acting by g(log t) = log t + log ε(g); ν_{B_pdR} is the unique B_dR-derivation with ν(log t) = −1, preserving B⁺_pdR and commuting with G_K. D_pdR(W) := (B_pdR ⊗_{B_dR} W)^{G_K} is a K-vector space with dim_K D_pdR(W) ≤ dim_{B_dR} W, and W is almost de Rham precisely when equality holds.

items.name: Fontaine’s equivalence: almost de Rham representations are pairs (V, ν)
items.statement: For a field E of characteristic 0, Rep_E(G_a) is equivalent to the category of pairs (V, ν_V) with ν_V nilpotent. D_pdR, with the G_a-action induced by ν_{B_pdR} ⊗ 1, induces an equivalence Rep_pdR(G_K) ≅ Rep_K(G_a); a quasi-inverse is (V,ν_V) ↦ (B_pdR ⊗_K V)^{ν⊗1+1⊗ν_V=0}, both functors are exact, and there is a comparison isomorphism ρ_pdR : B_pdR ⊗_K D_pdR(W) ≅ B_pdR ⊗_{B_dR} W (3.2).

items.name: The coefficient version of the equivalence
items.statement: For A a finite dimensional Q_p-algebra, an A⊗_{Q_p}B_dR-representation is a B_dR-representation with an A-action making it finite free over A⊗_{Q_p}B_dR. D_pdR induces an equivalence between the almost de Rham ones, Rep_{pdR,A}(G_K), and Rep_{A⊗_{Q_p}K}(G_a); in particular W is free over A⊗B_dR iff D_pdR(W) is free over A⊗K. Every A⊗B_dR-representation contains a B⁺_dR-lattice preserved by A.

items.name: The deformation groupoids X_W and X^□_W
items.statement: With G := Spec L ×_{Spec Q_p} Res_{K/Q_p}(GL_{n/K}) and g̃, X as in §2.1 over k = L: for W an almost de Rham L⊗B_dR-representation of rank n, X_W is the groupoid over C_L of triples (A,W_A,ι_A) deforming W, and X^□_W adds a framing α_A : (A⊗_{Q_p}K)^n ≅ D_pdR(W_A) lifting a fixed α. Any deformation of W is automatically almost de Rham. X^□_W → X_W is formally smooth and X^□_W → |X^□_W| is an equivalence, because a framed automorphism is the identity on D_pdR.

items.name: X^□_W is the completion of g at N_W
items.statement: The groupoid X^□_W is pro-representable and (W_A,ι_A,α_A) ↦ N_{W_A} — the matrix of α_A^{−1}∘ν_{W_A}∘α_A — identifies |X^□_W| with ĝ, the completion of g at N_W. In particular |X^□_W| is pro-represented by a power series ring in n²[K:Q_p] variables. The unframed |X_W| is not pro-representable, though it has a hull.

items.name: The filtered framed groupoid is the completion of g̃
items.statement: A filtered A⊗B_dR-representation (W,F_•) is one with an increasing filtration by subrepresentations whose graded pieces are free of rank one (Definition 3.1.8). For (W,F_•) with W almost de Rham, X_{W,F_•} and X^□_{W,F_•} := X_{W,F_•} ×_{X_W} X^□_W are defined; the functor (W_A,F_{A,•},ι_A,α_A) ↦ (α_A^{−1}(𝒟_{A,•}), N_{W_A}), with 𝒟_{A,i} = D_pdR(F_{A,i}), identifies |X^□_{W,F_•}| with the completion ĝ̃ of g̃ at (α^{−1}(𝒟_•), N_W), a formally smooth complete local ring of dimension n²[K:Q_p].

items.name: The weight morphism κ_{W,F_•}
items.statement: With κ : g̃ → t the weight map of §2.3, which sends (α^{−1}(𝒟_•),N_W) to 0 since N_W is nilpotent, κ_{W,F_•} is the composite X^□_{W,F_•} ≅ ĝ̃ → t̂; it factors through X_{W,F_•} → t̂ independently of the framing, and on points κ_{W,F_•}(x_A) = (ν_{A,1},…,ν_{A,n}) where ν_{A,i} is the endomorphism induced by ν_{W_A} on 𝒟_{A,i}/𝒟_{A,i−1} (3.4).

items.name: Lattices correspond to filtrations
items.statement: For W in Rep_pdR(G_K) and a G_K-stable B⁺_dR-lattice W⁺ ⊆ W, set Fil^i_{W⁺}(D_pdR(W)) := (t^iB⁺_pdR ⊗_{B⁺_dR} W⁺)^{G_K} (3.5); the i with non-zero graded piece are the opposites of the Sen weights of W⁺/tW⁺. The map W⁺ ↦ Fil^•_{W⁺}(D_pdR(W)) is a bijection between the G_K-stable B⁺_dR-lattices of W and the filtrations of D_pdR(W) as a G_a-representation.
items.note: Formula (3.6) in the proof prints D_dR(W) for D_pdR(W); see source issue E8.

items.name: The B⁺_dR-analogue of the coefficient equivalence
items.statement: W⁺ ↦ (D_pdR(W⁺[1/t]), Fil^•_{W⁺}) is an equivalence between almost de Rham A⊗_{Q_p}B⁺_dR-representations of G_K and filtered A⊗_{Q_p}K-representations of G_a — pairs (V, Fil^•) with Fil^• decreasing, exhaustive and separated by subobjects with free graded pieces. Moreover for any finite type A-module M there is a natural isomorphism M ⊗_A gr^i_{Fil^•_{W⁺}}(D_pdR(W⁺[1/t])) ≅ gr^i_{Fil^•_{M⊗_AW⁺}}(D_pdR(M⊗_AW⁺[1/t])).
items.note: The printed definition of a filtered representation requires the graded pieces to be free of rank one "for i ∈ Z", which is impossible for an exhaustive separated filtration; see source issue E8.

items.name: The graded pieces are constant in a deformation
items.statement: For A in C_L, W⁺_A an almost de Rham A⊗B⁺_dR-representation deforming W⁺, and every τ ∈ Σ and i ∈ Z, gr^i_{Fil^•_{W⁺_A}}(D_{pdR,τ}(W_A)) ⊗_A L ≅ gr^i_{Fil^•_{W⁺}}(D_{pdR,τ}(W)); in particular the non-zero graded pieces occur exactly at the i = −h_{τ,j}.

items.name: Regular lattices and the second description of ĝ̃
items.statement: W⁺ is regular if for each τ the integers h_{τ,i} are pairwise distinct. For W⁺ regular, Fil_{W⁺_A,i}(D_pdR(W_A)) := ⊕_{τ∈Σ} Fil^{−h_{τ,i}}_{W⁺_A}(D_{pdR,τ}(W_A)) (3.9) is a complete flag stable under ν_{W_A}, and (W⁺_A,ι_A,α_A) ↦ (α_A^{−1}(Fil_{W⁺_A,•}), N_{W_A}) identifies |X^□_{W⁺}| with the completion of g̃ at (α^{−1}(Fil_{W⁺,•}), N_W) — a different point of g̃(L) from the one in §3.1, the two being mixed in §3.5. The associated weight map is κ_{W⁺} : X_{W⁺} → t̂.
items.note: The completion point is printed without α^{−1}, and the weight map is said to use "the isomorphism of Corollary 3.2.5" where 3.2.5 is a Theorem; see source issue E8.

items.name: (φ,Γ_K)-modules over the Robba ring and after inverting t
items.statement: A (φ,Γ_K)-module over R_K[1/t] is a finite free R_K[1/t]-module with commuting semilinear φ and Γ_K-action admitting a (φ,Γ_K)-stable R_K-lattice; with A-coefficients one requires finite freeness over R_{A,K}[1/t]. The categories are written ΦΓ⁺_K, ΦΓ_K and ΦΓ_{A,K}. A module is of character type if it is isomorphic to R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t] for a continuous δ : K^× → A^×.

items.name: Algebraic, constant, smooth and locally algebraic characters
items.statement: A continuous δ : K^× → A^× is algebraic if δ(z) = ∏_{τ∈Σ} τ(z)^{k_τ}, written z^k; constant if it factors through L^×; smooth if wt(δ) = 0; and locally algebraic if it is a product of a smooth and an algebraic character, equivalently if wt_τ(δ) ∈ Z for all τ. With Lubin–Tate elements t_τ, every non-zero (φ,Γ_K)-submodule of R_{L,K}(δ)[1/t] over R_{L,K} is t^kR_{L,K}(δ) for some k ∈ Z^{[K:Q_p]}.

items.name: (φ,γ_K)-cohomology and its comparison with Ext groups
items.statement: H^i_{φ,γ_K}(M) is the cohomology of the Herr-type complex (3.10). For D ⊆ M with M = D[1/t], H^i_{φ,γ_K}(M) = colim_n H^i_{φ,γ_K}(t^{−n}D) (3.11), and H^1_{φ,γ_K}(M) ≅ Ext^1_{ΦΓ_K}(R_K[1/t],M) (3.12); the pull-back Ext^1_{ΦΓ_{A,K}}(R_{A,K}[1/t],M) → Ext^1_{ΦΓ_K}(R_K[1/t],M) is an isomorphism (3.13). H^0_{φ,γ_K} is left exact with H^0_{φ,γ_K}(R_{A,K}[1/t]) = A, and dim H^0_{φ,γ_K}(R_{A,K}(δ)) ≤ dim H^0_{φ,γ_K}(R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t]) ≤ dim A (3.14).

items.name: Cohomology of R_{L,K}(δ)/t^kR_{L,K}(δ)
items.statement: For k ∈ Z^{[K:Q_p]}_{≥0}, δ : K^× → L^× continuous and j ∈ {0,1}: if wt_τ(δ) ∉ {1−k_τ,…,0} for every τ then H^j_{φ,γ_K}(R_{L,K}(δ)/t^kR_{L,K}(δ)) = 0; if wt_τ(δ) ∈ {1−k_τ,…,0} for every τ then it has dimension [K:Q_p] over L.

items.name: Rigidity of the parameter after inverting t
items.statement: If R_{A,K}(δ₁)[1/t] ≅ R_{A,K}(δ₂)[1/t] then δ₂δ₁^{−1} is a constant algebraic character K^× → L^×.

items.name: The functors W⁺_dR and W_dR and their freeness
items.statement: W⁺_dR is Berger’s functor from (φ,Γ_K)-modules over R_K to B⁺_dR-representations, and W_dR(M) := B_dR ⊗_{B⁺_dR} W⁺_dR(D) for any D with M = D[1/t], independent of D. If D is of rank n over R_{A,K} then W⁺_dR(D) is finite free of rank n over A⊗_{Q_p}B⁺_dR, and if M is of rank n over R_{A,K}[1/t] then W_dR(M) is finite free of rank n over A⊗_{Q_p}B_dR. Both functors are exact.
items.locator: Lemma 3.3.5 with the following remark, printed pp. 344–345

items.name: When W_dR of a rank-one module is almost de Rham
items.statement: Let δ : K^× → A^× be continuous and M := R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t]. If δ̄ := δ mod m_A is smooth then W_dR(M) is almost de Rham with wt(δ) = ν_{W_dR(M)}; more generally if δ̄ is locally algebraic then W_dR(M) is almost de Rham with wt(δ) = wt(δ̄) + ν_{W_dR(M)}. Moreover W_dR(R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t]) is trivial if and only if δ is locally algebraic.

items.name: Trianguline modules, triangulations and parameters
items.statement: M in ΦΓ_{A,K} of rank n is trianguline if it has an increasing filtration M_• by subobjects with M_1 and the M_i/M_{i−1} of character type; M_• is a triangulation and the δ_i with M_i/M_{i−1} ≅ R_{A,K}(δ_i)[1/t] form a parameter. A triangulation is a filtration by direct factors, and by Lemma 3.3.4 either all parameters of M_• are locally algebraic or none is.

items.name: The deformation groupoids of a trianguline module and the character space
items.statement: X_{M,M_•} is the groupoid over C_L of deformations (M_A, M_{A,•}, j_A) of M with its triangulation, and X_M the version without the triangulation. T is the rigid space of continuous characters of K^×; the functor of deformations of a parameter δ is pro-represented by the completion T̂^n_δ of T^n_L at δ, and (M_A,M_{A,•},j_A) ↦ δ_A gives ω_δ : X_{M,M_•} → T̂^n_δ, with ω_{δ′} = (×δ′δ^{−1})∘ω_δ for another parameter (3.15). The framed versions are X^□_M := X_M ×_{X_W} X^□_W and X^□_{M,M_•} := X_{M,M_•} ×_{X_{W,F_•}} X^□_{W,F_•}.

items.name: Parameters and the ν-weight map agree
items.statement: Setting F_i := W_dR(M_i), if M_• has a locally algebraic parameter then W := W_dR(M) is almost de Rham with the filtration F_•, and the square formed by X_{M,M_•} → X_{W,F_•}, ω_δ, κ_{W,F_•} and wt − wt(δ) : T̂^n_δ → t̂ (3.16) commutes. Hence a morphism X_{M,M_•} → T̂^n_δ ×_{t̂} X_{W,F_•} (3.17).
items.note: Formula (3.16) is printed with the tuple index inside the difference; see source issue E8.

items.name: The comparison map from (φ,γ_K)-cohomology to Galois cohomology
items.statement: For W an almost de Rham A⊗B_dR-representation, Ext^1 in Rep_{pdR,A}(G_K) agrees with Ext^1 in all A⊗B_dR-representations and with H^1(G_K,W) (3.18); exactness of W_dR then gives a functorial A⊗K-linear map H^1_{φ,γ_K}(M) → H^1(G_K,W_dR(M)) (3.19). Through Fontaine’s equivalence, H^0(G_K,W) ≅ ker(ν_W) and H^1(G_K,W) ≅ coker(ν_W), so H^1(G_K,−) is right exact on Rep_pdR(G_K) and exact on de Rham representations.

items.name: Comparison of H¹ before and after inverting t
items.statement: Let δ : K^× → L^× be continuous with δ and εδ^{−1} not algebraic, and k ∈ Z^{[K:Q_p]}_{≥0}. Then H^0_{φ,γ_K}(t^{−k}R_{L,K}(δ)) = H^2_{φ,γ_K}(R_{L,K}(δ)) = 0; the map H^1_{φ,γ_K}(R_{L,K}(δ)) → H^1_{φ,γ_K}(t^{−k}R_{L,K}(δ)) is an isomorphism if wt_τ(δ) ∉ {1,…,k_τ} for all τ, and is zero if wt_τ(δ) ∈ {1,…,k_τ} for all τ. Both spaces have dimension [K:Q_p].

items.name: The comparison is an isomorphism in rank one
items.statement: For δ : K^× → L^× locally algebraic with δ and εδ^{−1} not algebraic, the map of (3.19) H^1_{φ,γ_K}(R_{L,K}(δ)[1/t]) → H^1(G_K, W_dR(R_{L,K}(δ)[1/t])) ≅ H^1(G_K, L⊗_{Q_p}B_dR) is an isomorphism.

items.name: The comparison over artinian coefficients
items.statement: Let A be in C_L and δ : K^× → A^× continuous with δ̄ and εδ̄^{−1} not algebraic. Then H^0_{φ,γ_K}(R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t]) = H^2_{φ,γ_K}(R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t]) = 0; if δ̄ is locally algebraic the comparison map to H^1(G_K, W_dR(R_{A,K}(δ)[1/t])) is surjective; and if δ itself is locally algebraic it is an isomorphism.

items.name: The genericity locus T_0 and T^n_0
items.statement: T_0 ⊂ T_L is the complement of the L-points z^k and ε(z)z^k, k ∈ Z^{[K:Q_p]}; T^n_0 consists of the δ = (δ_1,…,δ_n) with δ_i/δ_j ∈ T_0 for i ≠ j, i.e. the complement of those for which δ_iδ_j^{−1} OR εδ_iδ_j^{−1} is algebraic for SOME i ≠ j. If a triangulation admits a parameter in T^n_0(L) then all its parameters lie there.
items.note: The printed equivalent description says "δ_iδ_j^{−1} and εδ_iδ_j^{−1} are algebraic for i ≠ j", which can never hold, so as printed T^n_0 = T^n_L; see source issue E2. The statement above is the corrected one.

items.name: The key formal smoothness theorem
items.statement: Let M be trianguline of rank n over R_{L,K}[1/t] with triangulation M_• and parameter δ, and assume δ is locally algebraic and lies in T^n_0(L). With W := W_dR(M) and F_• := W_dR(M_•), the morphism X_{M,M_•} → T̂^n_δ ×_{t̂} X_{W,F_•} of (3.17) is formally smooth. The proof builds the deformation step by step, reducing to the surjectivity of a fibre-product map (3.23) via Lemma 3.4.3 and a base-change identity for H^1(G_K,−) coming from coker(ν).

items.name: A surjectivity lemma for fibre products of modules
items.statement: For a ring A, an ideal I with B := A/I and a surjection f : M ↠ N of A-modules, the map M → (M⊗_AB) ×_{N⊗_AB} N, m ↦ (m⊗1, f(m)), is surjective.

items.name: Forgetting the triangulation is a closed immersion
items.statement: A morphism of groupoids over C_L is a closed immersion if it is relatively representable and each representing map of complete local rings is a surjection. For M trianguline with triangulation M_• and parameter δ ∈ T^n_0(L), the morphism X_{M,M_•} → X_M is relatively representable and a closed immersion, because the deforming triangulation is unique.
items.locator: Proposition 3.4.6 with the preceding definition, printed p. 354

items.name: Vanishing ν forces the deformation to split
items.statement: Let M be trianguline with triangulation M_• and locally algebraic parameter δ ∈ T^n_0(L), and let (A,M_A,M_{A,•},j_A) be an object of X_{M,M_•} such that the nilpotent endomorphism ν_{W_dR(M_A)} vanishes. Then M_{A,i} = ⊕_{j≤i} R_{A,K}(δ_{A,j})[1/t] for every i, so M_A, and hence M, is split.

items.name: Deformations of a (φ,Γ_K)-module split into a t-inverted and a lattice part
items.statement: For D a (φ,Γ_K)-module over R_{L,K} with W⁺_dR(D) almost de Rham, the groupoid X_D of deformations of D is equivalent to X_{D[1/t]} ×_{X_{W_dR(D[1/t])}} X_{W⁺_dR(D)}. The proof rests on Berger’s equivalence between (φ,Γ_K)-modules over R_K and B-pairs, and on the rank-preserving equivalence between ΦΓ_{A,K} and A⊗_{Q_p}B_e-representations of G_K, B_e = B_cris^{φ=1}, given by M ↦ W_e(M) with quasi-inverse W_e ↦ D(W_e,W⁺_dR)[1/t].
items.locator: Proposition 3.5.1 and its proof, printed p. 355

items.name: Freeness criterion and existence of free lattices
items.statement: A (φ,Γ_K)-module D with an A-action is free over R_{A,K} if and only if D[1/t] is free over R_{A,K}[1/t] and W⁺_dR(D) is free over A⊗_{Q_p}B⁺_dR. Consequently any M in ΦΓ_{A,K} with W_dR(M) almost de Rham possesses a free R_{A,K}-lattice stable under φ and Γ_K.

items.name: The trianguline groupoids X_{D,M_•} and their framed and filtered companions
items.statement: For D trianguline of rank n with M := D[1/t] and a triangulation M_• possessing a locally algebraic parameter, put W⁺ := W⁺_dR(D), W := W_dR(M) and F_• := W_dR(M_•). Then X_{D,M_•} := X_D ×_{X_M} X_{M,M_•}, X^□_D := X_D ×_{X_W} X^□_W, X_{W⁺,F_•} := X_{W⁺} ×_{X_W} X_{W,F_•} and their framed versions are defined; in each of them one deforms the filtration on M = D[1/t], resp. on W = W⁺[1/t], and not a triangulation on D itself.

items.name: Relative representability of the comparison morphisms
items.statement: Under the running hypotheses (D trianguline, M_• with a parameter in T^n_0(L)), the morphisms X_M → X_W and X_{M,M_•} → X_{W,F_•} are relatively representable, and so are X^□_{M,M_•} → X^□_{W,F_•}, X_{D,M_•} → X_{W⁺,F_•} and X^□_{D,M_•} → X^□_{W⁺,F_•}.

items.name: Formal smoothness of the comparison morphisms
items.statement: The morphism wt − wt(δ) : T̂^n_δ → t̂ is formally smooth of relative dimension n (Lemma 3.5.5), and hence the morphisms X_{M,M_•} → X_{W,F_•}, X^□_{M,M_•} → X^□_{W,F_•}, X_{D,M_•} → X_{W⁺,F_•} and X^□_{D,M_•} → X^□_{W⁺,F_•} are formally smooth.

items.name: Pro-representability and dimension of the framed trianguline groupoid
items.statement: X^□_{M,M_•} is pro-representable and |X^□_{M,M_•}| is pro-represented by a formally smooth complete local ring of residue field L and dimension [K:Q_p](n² + n(n+1)/2). The proof uses the rigidified groupoid X^ver_{M,M_•}, in which the isomorphisms of the graded pieces are also deformed; it is pro-represented by a formally smooth ring of dimension n + [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2.
items.locator: Proposition 3.5.7 and its proof, printed pp. 358–359

items.name: The framed filtered lattice groupoid is the completion of X at x_pdR
items.statement: With W⁺ regular, put x := (α^{−1}(𝒟_•), α^{−1}(Fil_{W⁺,•}), N_W) ∈ X(L), the triple of the two flags and the nilpotent operator. Then X^□_{W⁺,F_•} is pro-representable with |X^□_{W⁺,F_•}| ≅ X̂_x, and X^□_{D,M_•} is pro-representable and formally smooth of relative dimension [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 over X̂_x.

items.name: The w-components and the set S(x)
items.statement: For w in the Weyl group S, X^{□,w}_{W⁺,F_•} := X^□_{W⁺,F_•} ×_{|X^□_{W⁺,F_•}|} X̂_{w,x} (3.25), and X^w_{W⁺,F_•} is its image under forgetting the framing, independent of α by G-equivariance of X_w (3.26); similarly X^{□,w}_{D,M_•} and X^w_{D,M_•}. Then |X^{□,w}_{W⁺,F_•}| ≅ X̂_{w,x}, these morphisms are closed immersions, and S(x) := {w : x ∈ X_w(L)} = {w : X^w_{D,M_•} ≠ 0}.
items.note: The proof of Proposition 3.5.10 prints an object of X^□_{W⁺,F_•}(A) with an undefined entry "F_W" in place of the deformed filtration F_{A,•}; see source issue E9.

items.name: Each w-component is a normal domain
items.statement: For w ∈ S(x), X^{□,w}_{D,M_•} is pro-representable by a complete local normal domain of residue field L and dimension [K:Q_p](n² + n(n+1)/2), formally smooth over X̂_{w,x}. This is where the normality of X_w (Theorem 2.3.6) is used, together with the stability of normal domains under completion for excellent local rings.

items.name: The map Θ detects which component a deformation lies on
items.statement: The map (κ₁,κ₂) induces X̂_x → T̂_{(0,0)} and X̂_{w,x} → T̂_{w,(0,0)}, and Θ denotes the resulting morphism X_{D,M_•} → T̂_{(0,0)}, independent of the framing. For w ∈ S(x) and w′ ∈ S, the morphisms induced by Θ on X^{□,w}_{D,M_•} and on X^w_{D,M_•} factor through T̂_{w′,(0,0)} if and only if w′ = w.

items.name: Galois deformation groupoids and the trianguline ones
items.statement: For r : G_K → GL_n(L) continuous with associated representation V, X_r is the groupoid of deformations of r and X_V that of deformations of V; X_r → X_V is relatively representable and formally smooth of relative dimension n², and D_rig induces X_V ≅ X_D for D := D_rig(V). For V trianguline with a triangulation M_• of M := D[1/t], one sets X_{V,M_•} := X_V ×_{X_D} X_{D,M_•} and X_{r,M_•} := X_r ×_{X_V} X_{V,M_•}, with framed versions; the framing □ is on D_pdR(B_dR ⊗ V), not directly on the Galois deformation, and all automorphisms in these groupoids are trivial.

items.name: Structure of the trianguline Galois deformation ring
items.statement: Assume V trianguline with a triangulation M_• admitting a locally algebraic parameter in T^n_0(L), W⁺ = B⁺_dR ⊗ V regular, and x ∈ X(L) as above. (i) |X_{r,M_•}| is pro-represented by a reduced equidimensional complete local ring R_{r,M_•} of dimension n² + [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2. (ii) For w ∈ S(x), |X^w_{r,M_•}| is pro-represented by R_{r,M_•}/p_w with p_w a minimal prime and the quotient normal, and w ↦ p_w is a bijection from S(x) onto the minimal primes of R_{r,M_•}. (iii) The composite of Θ with |X^w_{r,M_•}| factors through T̂_{w′,(0,0)} if and only if w′ = w.

items.name: Tangent-space dimension of the w-component
items.statement: For w ∈ S(x), dim_L X^w_{r,M_•}(L[ε]) = n² − [K:Q_p]n² + [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 + dim_L T_{X_w,x}.

items.name: The Bruhat constraint from the relative position of the two flags
items.statement: Let w_x ∈ S be the relative position of the pair of flags (α^{−1}(𝒟_•), α^{−1}(Fil_{W⁺,•})), independent of α. If w ∈ S(x), equivalently X^w_{r,M_•} ≠ 0, then w_x ≼ w.

items.name: The trianguline variety
items.statement: T_reg ⊂ T_L is the complement of the z^{−k} and ε(z)z^k with k ∈ Z^Σ_{≥0}, and T^n_reg the locus where δ_i/δ_j ∈ T_reg for i ≠ j; T^n_0 ⊊ T^n_reg. For r̄ : G_K → GL_n(k_L) with framed deformation ring R_r̄ and 𝔛_r̄ := (Spf R_r̄)^rig, the trianguline variety X_tri(r̄) is the Zariski closure in 𝔛_r̄ × T^n_L of U_tri(r̄) := {(r,δ) ∈ 𝔛_r̄ × T^n_reg : r is trianguline of parameter δ} (3.29). It is reduced and equidimensional of dimension n² + [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2, with U_tri(r̄) Zariski-open, and ω′ denotes the projection to T^n_L.

items.name: Uniqueness of the triangulation of a given generic parameter
items.statement: If δ ∈ T^n_0 then the (φ,Γ_K)-module M over R_{L,K}[1/t] has a unique triangulation of parameter δ.

items.name: The completed local ring of the trianguline variety embeds in the deformation groupoid
items.statement: There is a canonical isomorphism X_r ≅ 𝔛̂_{r̄,r} and hence a morphism X̂_tri(r̄)_x → X_r; it factors through X_{r,M_•} (Proposition 3.7.2, via the global triangulation of [49, Cor. 6.3.10] after a proper birational modification), and both X̂_tri(r̄)_x → X_{r,M_•} and X̂_tri(r̄)_x → X_r are closed immersions.

items.name: The weight permutation and the component reached by Θ
items.statement: For x = (r,δ) with δ locally algebraic and W⁺ regular, let h_{τ,1} < … < h_{τ,n} be the Sen weights of r and let w = (w_τ)_τ ∈ S be defined by wt_τ(δ_{w_τ(i)}) = h_{τ,i}. Then the composite Θ_x : X̂_tri(r̄)_x → T̂_{(0,0)} factors through T̂_{w,(0,0)}. The proof compares the two weight maps through the Sen polynomial: the graded comparison (3.31), the computation of the Sen polynomial of an almost de Rham lattice (Lemma 3.7.5), the Sen polynomial of the deformation (Lemma 3.7.6) and a root-matching lemma over a local ring (Lemma 3.7.7).
items.note: The first display in the proof of Lemma 3.7.4 prints "wt_τ(δ_i)_{τ∈Σ}" without the inner parentheses; see source issue E9.

items.name: The trianguline variety is a single component of the deformation ring
items.statement: The closed immersion X̂_tri(r̄)_x ↪ X_{r,M_•} induces an isomorphism X̂_tri(r̄)_x ≅ X^w_{r,M_•}, w being the weight permutation of Lemma 3.7.4.

items.name: The standing hypotheses on the point x, and their crystalline sufficient condition
items.statement: The assumptions on x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(r̄)(L) are: δ locally algebraic; δ_iδ_j^{−1} and εδ_iδ_j^{−1} not algebraic for i ≠ j; and the τ-Sen weights of the representation attached to r distinct for each τ. They hold whenever the representation is crystalline with distinct Hodge–Tate weights for each τ and the eigenvalues φ_i of φ^{[K_0:Q_p]} on D_cris satisfy φ_iφ_j^{−1} ∉ {1, p^{[K_0:Q_p]}} for i ≠ j.

items.name: The local model diagram
items.statement: For x = (r,δ) satisfying Remark 3.7.9 there is a commutative diagram (3.33) of formal schemes over L whose top row is X̂_tri(r̄)_x ≅ X^w_{r,M_•} ← X^{□,w}_{r,M_•} → X^{□,w}_{V,M_•} ≅ X^{□,w}_{D,M_•} → X^{□,w}_{W⁺,F_•} ≅ X̂_{w,x_pdR}, with middle and bottom rows the unframed and unfiltered analogues; every horizontal morphism which is not an isomorphism is formally smooth, every vertical morphism is a closed immersion and every square is cartesian. This is the local model theorem announced as Theorem 1.6.

items.name: Local normality and Cohen–Macaulayness of the trianguline variety
items.statement: Let x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(r̄) satisfy the assumptions of Remark 3.7.9. Then X_tri(r̄) is normal, hence irreducible, and Cohen–Macaulay at x. This follows from Theorem 3.6.2(ii), Proposition 2.3.3 and the diagram (3.33).

items.name: Flatness of the character map at such points
items.statement: For x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(r̄) satisfying Remark 3.7.9, the morphism ω′ : X_tri(r̄) → T^n_L is flat in a neighbourhood of x; the same then holds for the weight map ω to W^n_L. On the Zariski-open U_tri(r̄) the map ω′ is even smooth, but it can be ramified in general.
items.locator: Proposition 4.1.1 with the following paragraph, printed pp. 371–373

items.name: The accumulation property
items.statement: X_tri(r̄) satisfies the accumulation property at a point x with ω(x) algebraic and satisfying Remark 3.7.9: for every C > 0 the crystalline strictly dominant points with pairwise distinct Frobenius eigenvalues, non-critical, and with consecutive weight gaps greater than C accumulate at x.

items.name: Tangent space of the trianguline variety at a de Rham point
items.statement: Let x = (r,δ) satisfy Remark 3.7.9 with r de Rham, and let d_{w′} be the rank of the lattice generated by the w′(α) − α. Then (i) dim T_{X_tri(r̄),x} = dim X_tri(r̄) − [K:Q_p]n² + dim T_{X_w,x_pdR}, so X_tri(r̄) is smooth at x if and only if X_w is smooth at x_pdR; and (ii) dim T_{X_tri(r̄),x} ≤ dim X_tri(r̄) − d_{ww_x^{−1}} + lg(w_xw_0) + dim T_{Ū_w,π(x_pdR)} − [K:Q_p]n(n−1). In particular if π(x_pdR) is a smooth point of Ū_w and d_{ww_x^{−1}} = lg(w) − lg(w_x), then X_tri(r̄) is smooth at x.

items.name: The strictly dominant case and the comparison with the authors’ earlier bound
items.statement: When w = w_0 the smoothness hypothesis on π(x_pdR) is automatic and (4.1) dim T_{X_tri(r̄),x} ≤ dim X_tri(r̄) − d_{w_xw_0} + lg(w_xw_0), which is exactly the bound of [20, Th. 1.3] once one notes that the permutation w_x here is w_x^{old}w_0 in the notation of loc. cit. Both hypotheses of (ii) hold when lg(w) − lg(w_x) ≤ 2. Granting Conjecture 2.3.7 for w = w_0, (4.1) is an equality, which implies [20, Conj. 2.8].

items.name: Local companion points
items.statement: For x = (r,δ) with r de Rham with distinct Hodge–Tate weights h and wt(δ) = w_0(h) (strict dominance), a companion point of x is an x′ = (r,δ′) ∈ X_tri(r̄) with δ′_i/δ_i algebraic for every i; then wt(δ′) = w′(h) for some w′ ∈ S. When r is crystalline, a refinement φ is an ordering of the eigenvalues of φ^{[K_0:Q_p]} on D_cris(r), δ = z^{w_0(h)}unr(φ), and every companion point has the form (r, z^{w(h)}unr(φ)).
items.locator: Definition 4.2.1 with the surrounding text, printed p. 375
items.note: Two notational slips in this passage — a free index in the definition of z^h, and wt_τ where wt is meant; see source issue E10.

items.name: All local companion points in the crystalline case
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of §4.2 — r̄ fixed, x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(r̄) with r crystalline, Hodge–Tate weights distinct, δ = z^{w_0(h)}unr(φ) strictly dominant and φ_iφ_j^{−1} ∉ {1, p^{[K_0:Q_p]}} for i ≠ j — the set of companion points of x is exactly {x_w := (r, z^{w(h)}unr(φ)) : w_x ≼ w}. The necessity of w_x ≼ w comes from Corollary 3.7.8 and Proposition 3.6.4; the existence of every x_w with w ≽ w_x is proved by a Zariski-density argument inside the space of crystalline points, and does not use the local model. The paper presents this as the local analogue of [16, Conj. 6.6]. An analogue holds for r merely de Rham.

items.name: Cycles on the framed deformation ring and the two fibres
items.statement: For r ∈ 𝔛_r̄(L), Ô_{𝔛_r̄,r} represents the framed deformations of r and has dimension n² + [K:Q_p]n². X_tri(r̄)_δ is the fibre of ω′ at δ and X_tri(r̄)_{wt(δ)} the fibre of the weight map. Taking completions in (3.33) and then fibres over 0 ∈ t gives the diagram (4.6), whose components are indexed by the components of the Steinberg variety through x_pdR; one obtains cycles 𝖅_{w′} of codimension [K:Q_p]n(n+1)/2 and 𝕮_{w′} := Σ_{w″} a_{w′,w″}𝖅_{w″} (4.7), independent of the framing. Taking instead the fibre at δ gives (4.11) and cycles 𝒵_{w′}, 𝒞_{w′} of codimension [K:Q_p]n(n+3)/2 (4.12).
items.note: The two families of cycles are distinguished in the printed text only by font; any formalisation must name them apart.

items.name: Identification of the top cycle with the crystalline deformation cycle
items.statement: If r is crystalline with Hodge–Tate weights given by wt(δ) and δ ∈ T^n_0, then 𝕮_{w_0} = 𝖅_{w_0} corresponds to an irreducible closed subscheme of Spec Ô of the crystalline deformation space of dimension n² + [K:Q_p]n(n−1)/2, and since that space is already irreducible of this dimension, 𝕮_{w_0} ≅ [Spec Ô_{𝔛^{wt(δ)−cr}_r̄,r}] (4.8). Moreover r is de Rham if and only if 𝖅_{w_0} ≠ 0.

items.name: The weight fibre as a Kazhdan–Lusztig combination
items.statement: For x = (r,δ) ∈ X_tri(r̄)(L) with the unique triangulation of parameter δ and w with wt(δ) = w(h), [Spec Ô_{X_tri(r̄)_{wt(δ)},x}] = Σ_{w′∈S} P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1)𝕮_{w′}. More precisely the sum runs over w_{x_pdR} ≼ w′ ≼ w (4.9), and when r is de Rham every term is non-zero.
items.note: The statement of Corollary 4.3.2 is printed with a broken clause ("Let M_• be … and that w ∈ S is such that …"); see source issue E10.

items.name: The locally analytic Breuil–Mézard type conjecture
items.statement: CONJECTURE (Conjecture 4.3.4, not proved in general). For every generic trianguline r ∈ 𝔛_r̄(L) and every absolutely irreducible constituent Π of a locally Q_p-analytic principal series of GL_n(K), there is a unique cycle C_{r,Π} of codimension [K:Q_p]n(n+3)/2 in Z(Spec Ô_{𝔛_r̄,r}) with [Spec Ô_{X_tri(r̄)_δ,(r,δ)}] = Σ_Π m_{δ,Π}C_{r,Π} for every δ, the left-hand side being 0 when (r,δ) ∉ X_tri(r̄). It implies that the fibre is equidimensional of dimension n² + [K:Q_p]n(n−3)/2 when non-zero, and determines which (r,δ) lie on X_tri(r̄).
items.note: A conjecture; only uniqueness (Proposition 4.3.6) and the generic crystalline case (Theorem 4.3.8) are proved.

items.name: Uniqueness of the cycles
items.statement: For r generic trianguline with integral τ-Sen weights, the cycles C_{r,Π} of Conjecture 4.3.4, if they exist, are unique. The proof uses that a point of X_tri(r̄) has locally algebraic parameter in T^n_0, that each constituent occurs with multiplicity one in a suitable principal series, and descending induction along the strong linkage order.
items.locator: Proposition 4.3.6 with the preceding description of the constituents, printed pp. 381–382

items.name: The cycle depends only on r and the constituent
items.statement: With the notation of (4.12), the cycle 𝒞_{w′} depends only on r and on the constituent Π_{w′}, not on the chosen triangulation. The proof uses that the components of the Steinberg variety occurring in the characteristic cycle are stabilised by the parabolic P_{w′} (Remark 2.4.9) together with Lemma 3.4.7.

items.name: The conjecture holds for generic crystalline r
items.statement: Assume r ∈ 𝔛_r̄(L) is generic crystalline with distinct τ-Sen weights for every τ — equivalently crystalline with distinct Hodge–Tate weights and φ_iφ_j^{−1} ∉ {1, p^{[K_0:Q_p]}} for i ≠ j. Then Conjecture 4.3.4 holds for r, with C_{r,Π_{w′}} := 𝒞_{w′}; the consistency across different characters uses Theorem 4.2.3, and the final identity [Spec Ô_{X_tri(r̄)_δ,(r,δ)}] = Σ_{w′} P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1)𝒞_{w′} matches the multiplicities m_{δ,Π_{w′}} = P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1). The constituents that occur are exactly the companion constituents of [15, §6].

items.name: The global setting of §5
items.statement: Assume p > 2. F⁺ is totally real, F a totally imaginary quadratic extension splitting at all places above p, G a unitary group in n ≥ 2 variables over F⁺ with G ×_{F⁺} F ≅ GL_{n/F}, G(F⁺⊗_Q R) compact and G quasi-split at every finite place of F⁺. For each v ∈ S_p a place ṽ of F above v is fixed, giving i_ṽ : G(F⁺_v) ≅ GL_n(F_ṽ); K_v, B_v, B̄_v, T_v are the preimages of the integral, upper triangular, lower triangular and diagonal subgroups, and L is large enough to split every F⁺_v.

items.name: Completed cohomology, the Hecke algebra and the deformation ring
items.statement: For a tame level U^p, Ŝ(U^p,L) is the Banach space of continuous functions G(F⁺)\G(A^∞_{F⁺})/U^p → L with the unitary G_p-action, Ŝ(U^p,L)^an its very strongly admissible locally Q_p-analytic vectors. S is a finite set of finite places split in F containing S_p and the places where U_v is not maximal, T^S the spherical Hecke algebra, and m^S a maximal ideal with Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S} ≠ 0; ρ̄ is the associated absolutely semisimple Galois representation, assumed absolutely irreducible, and R_{ρ̄,S} pro-represents the deformations unramified outside S satisfying ρ^∨∘c ≅ ρ ⊗ ε^{n−1}.
items.note: The localised completed cohomology is printed as an inverse limit of O_L/m^s-valued functions, i.e. an O_L-module, where the L-Banach space is meant; see source issue E11.

items.name: The Hecke eigenvariety and the map to the trianguline varieties
items.statement: Y(U^p,ρ̄) is the schematic support of the coherent sheaf (J_{B_p}(Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S}))^∨ on X_{ρ̄,S} × T̂_{p,L}, with J_{B_p} Emerton’s Jacquet functor: a reduced rigid variety of dimension n[F⁺:Q], closed in X_{ρ̄,S} × T̂_{p,L}, whose points are the (ρ,δ) with a non-zero Hom from δ into the Jacquet module. With the twist ι_v(δ_1,…,δ_n) := δ_{B_v}·(δ_1, δ_2ε, …, δ_nε^{n−1}) (5.1) there is a morphism Y(U^p,ρ̄) → X_tri(ρ̄_p) = ∏_{v∈S_p} X_tri(ρ̄_ṽ) (5.2).

items.name: De Rham and crystalline strictly dominant points, and classicality
items.statement: x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) is de Rham (resp. crystalline) strictly dominant if every ρ_ṽ is de Rham (resp. crystalline) and the image of x in each X_tri(ρ̄_ṽ) is strictly dominant, equivalently wt_τ(δ_{v,i}) ≥ wt_τ(δ_{v,i+1}) for all i, τ, v. With F^{G_p}_{B̄_p}(δ) the Orlik–Strauch representation (5.3) and LA(δ) its maximal locally algebraic quotient (5.4), membership in Y(U^p,ρ̄) is equivalent to a non-zero Hom from F^{G_p}_{B̄_p}(δ) (5.5), and x is classical when such a morphism factors through LA(δ), equivalently when ρ comes from a classical automorphic representation.

items.name: The classicality conjecture
items.statement: CONJECTURE (Conjecture 5.1.1). Every de Rham strictly dominant point of Y(U^p,ρ̄) is classical.
items.note: A conjecture; Theorem 5.1.3 proves the generic crystalline case.

items.name: Classicality of generic crystalline strictly dominant points
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ unramified, ᵖ√1 ∉ F, U_v hyperspecial at the places inert in F and ρ̄(G_{F(ᵖ√1)}) adequate. Let x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) be crystalline strictly dominant with φ_{ṽ,i}φ_{ṽ,j}^{−1} ∉ {1, q_v} for i ≠ j and v ∈ S_p. Then x is classical. The proof passes to the patched eigenvariety and uses Corollary 3.7.10 at each place: local irreducibility supplies the unique component through the image of x, which is exactly the hypothesis of the classicality criterion of [20, Th. 3.9].

items.name: Automorphy without strict dominance
items.statement: If x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) satisfies the hypotheses of Theorem 5.1.3 but is not strictly dominant, there is a strictly dominant x′ = (ρ,δ′) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄), which is classical by Theorem 5.1.3; hence ρ is automorphic, although x itself need not be classical. Under the same hypotheses the crystalline assumption should be relaxable to crystabelline genericity.

items.name: The patched eigenvariety and its component decomposition
items.statement: With R_∞ the maximal reduced Z_p-flat quotient of (⊗̂_{v∈S}R_{ρ̄_ṽ})[[x_1,…,x_g]] and X_∞ = X_{ρ̄^p} × X_{ρ̄_p} × U^g, the patched representation Π_∞ of [23] and the ideal a with Π_∞[a] ≅ Ŝ(U^p,L)_{m^S} give the patched eigenvariety X_p(ρ̄), the support of (J_{B_p}(Π_∞^{R_∞−an}))^∨ (5.7); Y(U^p,ρ̄) is the closed subspace cut out by a. For each irreducible component X^p of X_{ρ̄^p} there is a union X^{X^p−aut}_tri(ρ̄_p) of components of X_tri(ρ̄_p) with X_p(ρ̄) ≅ ⋃_{X^p}(X^p × ι(X^{X^p−aut}_tri(ρ̄_p)) × U^g) (5.8).

items.name: The adjunction between Orlik–Strauch induction and Lie-algebra homomorphisms
items.statement: For Π^an very strongly admissible, M in category O and V a smooth representation of T_p, Hom_{G_p}(F^{G_p}_{B̄_p}(Hom(M,L)^{ū∞}, V(δ_{B_p}^{−1})), Π^an) ≅ Hom_{T_p⁺}(V, Hom_{U(g)}(M,Π^an)^{U_0}) functorially in M, where Hom_{U(g)}(M,Π^an)^{U_0} carries the Hecke action (5.9). Specialised to irreducible constituents and to Verma modules this gives Hom_{G_p}(F^{G_p}_{B̄_p}(L̄(−ν), 1[s]_smε_smδ_{B_p}^{−1}), Π^an) ≅ Hom_{U(g)}(L(ν),Π^an)^{U_0}[m^s_{ε_sm}] and the analogous statement for U(g)⊗_{U(b)}μ, the latter space being finite dimensional.

items.name: Finite dimensionality for an arbitrary object of category O
items.statement: For any object M of category O and any s ≥ 1, Hom_{U(g)}(M, Π^an)^{U_0}[m^s_{ε_sm}] is finite dimensional. This follows from the Verma case together with left exactness, the fact that every simple object of O is a quotient of a Verma module, and finite length in O.
items.note: Lemma 5.2.4 is printed as a verbatim repetition of the first assertion of Lemma 5.2.3, i.e. for the Verma module rather than for an arbitrary M; its proof gives the statement recorded here. See source issue E4.

items.name: Exactness criteria for the Hom functor on category O
items.statement: If the continuous dual Π′ is a finite projective O_L[[K_p]][1/p]-module then M ↦ Hom_{U(g)}(M,Π^an) is exact on finite type U(g)-modules (Lemma 5.2.5). Assuming that exactness (5.10) and that Π^an is the locally analytic vectors of a continuous admissible representation, the functor Hom_{U(g)}(−,Π^an)^{U_0}[m^∞_{ε_sm}] is exact on category O (Lemma 5.2.6).

items.name: A combinatorial lemma on the Bruhat order
items.statement: If lg(w) ≤ lg(w_0) − 2 there are exactly two elements w_1, w_2 with w ≼ w_i ≼ w_3, lg(w_i) = lg(w)+1 and lg(w_3) = lg(w)+2 for a third element w_3.

items.name: Refinements, companion characters and the permutation w_R
items.statement: Fix ρ ∈ X_{ρ̄,S} coming from a classical point of Y(U^p,ρ̄), with Hodge–Tate weights h_{ṽ,τ,1} < … < h_{ṽ,τ,n} and λ defined by λ_{v,τ,i} = h_{ṽ,τ,n+1−i} + i − 1, and assume each ρ_ṽ crystabelline generic, i.e. the Weil-group representation ⊕_i η_{ṽ,i} attached to ρ_ṽ satisfies (η_{ṽ,i}^{−1}η_{ṽ,j})∘rec ∉ {1, |·|} for i ≠ j. A refinement R orders the η_{ṽ,i} at each place; δ_{R,w} is the associated character (5.13), with derivative ww_0·λ and smooth part independent of w, and R ↦ (ρ,δ_{R,w_0}) is a bijection between refinements and classical points of Y(U^p,ρ̄) of the form (ρ,δ). w_R is the permutation attached to the image of (ρ,δ_{R,w_0}) in the trianguline varieties.

items.name: The companion constituent conjecture
items.statement: CONJECTURE (Conjecture 5.3.1, a case of [16, Conj. 6.1]). For a refinement R and w ∈ ∏_{v∈S_p}S_n^{[F_ṽ:Q_p]}, Hom_{G_p}(F^{G_p}_{B̄_p}(L̄(−ww_0·λ), δ_{R,sm}δ_{B_p}^{−1}), Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S}[m_ρ]) ≠ 0 if and only if w_R ≼ w. It is stronger than predicting the companion points of x, since it also determines which (ρ, z^μδ_{R,sm}) lie on the eigenvariety.

items.name: All expected companion constituents exist in the crystalline case
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ unramified, ᵖ√1 ∉ F, U^p small enough with U_v hyperspecial at the inert places and ρ̄(G_{F(ᵖ√1)}) adequate. Let ρ ∈ X_{ρ̄,S} come from a classical point of Y(U^p,ρ̄) with every ρ_ṽ crystalline and φ_{ṽ,i}φ_{ṽ,j}^{−1} ∉ {1, q_v} for i ≠ j and v ∈ S_p. Then Conjecture 5.3.1 holds for ρ. The necessity of w_R ≼ w comes from Theorem 4.2.3; the existence is a descending induction on the length, run on the patched eigenvariety, whose inductive step compares two cycle identities.

items.name: The two cycle identities of the induction
items.statement: For a suitable point y of the patched space with Weyl element w_y, writing L(w′w_0·μ) for the dual of Hom_{U(g)}(L(w′w_0·μ), Π^an_∞[m^∞_{r_y}])^{U_0}[m^∞_{ε_{w,sm}}] and M(ww_0·μ) for the pull-back of M_∞ to the weight fibre, one has in Z^d(Spec Ô_{X_∞,r_y}) with d = [F⁺:Q]n(n+1)/2: [M(ww_0·μ)] = Σ_{w_y ≼ w′ ≼ w} P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1)[L(w′w_0·μ)] (5.23) and [Ô_{X_p(ρ̄)_{ww_0·μ},y_w}] = Σ_{w_y ≼ w′ ≼ w} P_{w_0w,w_0w′}(1)C_{w′} (5.24), where C_{w′} is the pull-back of the product over v ∈ S_p of the local cycles of §4.3 and is non-zero in that range. The induction hypothesis also asserts that the rank of M_∞ near each companion point y_w is the same integer m_y.
items.locator: Proof of Theorem 5.3.3, Steps 3–6, formulas (5.23)–(5.24), printed pp. 397–400
items.note: The Claim of Step 3 is printed with the condition "w_R ≼ w", but w_R is defined only for a refinement of the fixed global ρ while y is a general point; the induction proves it with w_y ≼ w. See source issue E3.

items.name: Expected strengthenings of the companion theorem
items.statement: The authors expect that the crystalline hypothesis can be dropped, keeping crystabelline genericity, and that under the same hypotheses every irreducible locally Q_p-analytic subquotient C of a principal series with Hom_{G_p}(C, Ŝ(U^p,L)^an_{m^S}[m_ρ]) ≠ 0 is one of the constituents of (5.12) for some refinement and some w ≽ w_R. Special cases were known before: GL_2(Q_p) for completed H¹ of modular curves, Ding’s results for n = 2, and partial results for GL_n(Q_p).
items.note: Expectations, not theorems. The printed text of (i) writes the ideal as p_ρ, which is never defined; see source issue E11.

items.name: The eigenvariety is locally the fibre of the patched eigenvariety
items.statement: Under the hypotheses of Theorem 5.1.3, the map Y(U^p,ρ̄) → X_p(ρ̄) ×_{(Spf S_∞)^rig} Sp L (5.38) is an isomorphism of rigid spaces in a neighbourhood of a crystalline strictly dominant x with generic Frobenius eigenvalues; in particular that fibre product is reduced at such a point. The proof notes that Ô_{X_p(ρ̄),x} is the completed local ring of X_{ρ̄^p} × ι(X_tri(ρ̄_p)) × U^g by Corollary 3.7.10, so X_p(ρ̄) is Cohen–Macaulay at x, and records that the argument of [19, Th. 4.8] needs that Cohen–Macaulayness, which was overlooked in the proof of [20, Cor. 5.18].
items.note: The parenthesis of this proof is the authors’ own correction to their earlier paper [20]; recorded in the report and the errata log rather than as a source issue of this paper.

items.name: Cohen–Macaulayness, flatness of the weight map, and singularity
items.statement: Assume F/F⁺ unramified, ᵖ√1 ∉ F, U^p small enough with U_v hyperspecial at the inert places and ρ̄(G_{F(ᵖ√1)}) adequate. Let x = (ρ,δ) ∈ Y(U^p,ρ̄) be crystalline strictly dominant with φ_{ṽ,i}φ_{ṽ,j}^{−1} ∉ {1, q_v} for i ≠ j and v ∈ S_p. Then Y(U^p,ρ̄) is Cohen–Macaulay at x and the weight map Y(U^p,ρ̄) → T̂^0_{p,L} is flat at x; and if w_xw_0 is not a product of distinct simple reflections then Y(U^p,ρ̄) is singular at x. The singularity comes from the tangent-space computation dim T_{X_tri(ρ̄_p),x_p} = lg(w_xw_0) − d_{w_xw_0} + dim X_tri(ρ̄_p) (5.39) together with the fact that d_w < lg(w) exactly when w is not such a product.

items.name: What is left open at the companion points
items.statement: The same argument shows that if X_p(ρ̄) is singular at a companion point x_w then so is Y(U^p,ρ̄); which companion points are singular for w ≠ w_0 is left open and is related to Conjecture 2.3.7. Equality (5.39) shows that the tangent-space dimension of X_tri(ρ̄_ṽ) at the image of x is as predicted by [20, Conj. 2.8], so that conjecture holds at many points. When w_xw_0 is a product of distinct simple reflections, work of Bergdall leads one to expect that Y(U^p,ρ̄) is smooth at x; the method of this paper gives no information there.
